Gold(I)-catalysed [2+4] cycloaddition of
1,1-difluoroallenes with conjugated
enones: synthesis of ring-difluorinated
dihydro-2H-pyrans†
Daisuke Miyazaki,<sup>a</sup> Reo Eto,<sup>a</sup> Junji Ichikawa <sup>b</sup> and Kohei Fuchibe *<sup>a</sup>
rsc.li/chemcomm
1,1-Difluoroallenes underwent regioselective [2+4] cycloaddition with
a,b-unsaturated ketones (enones) in the presence of an AuCl(IPr)–
AgSbF catalyst. b-Aurated, charge-localized difluoroallylic carboca-
tions, formed from 1,1-difluoroallenes and the cationic Au catalyst,
were stabilised by the two fluorine substituents. This facilitated
a-selective nucleophilic attack by the enone oxygen, followed by six-
membered ring closure, leading to the formation of ring-difluorinated
dihydro-2H-pyrans with (E)-alkylidene groups in high yields.
1,1-Difluoroallenes
[ \mathbf { R } ( \mathbf { R } ^ { \prime } ) \mathbf { C } { \mathrm { = } } \mathbf { C } { \mathrm { = } } \mathbf { C } \mathbf { F } _ { 2 } ] ,
characterised by two
fluorine substituents on a cumulated diene framework, have
emerged as highly versatile synthetic building blocks for both
cyclic and acyclic organofluorine compounds.<sup>1,2</sup> The unique
properties of the fluorine substituents,<sup>3</sup> combined with the
reactive nature of the allene scafold,<sup>4</sup> enable pathways to
valuable fluorinated targets. Over the past decade, the synthetic
potential of 1,1-difluoroallenes has been extensively explored,
particularly through metal-catalysed or -promoted additions
and substitutions. For instance, additions involving carbon
and heteroatom<sup>6</sup> nucleophiles have facilitated the synthesis of
diverse difluorovinylic and difluoroallylic compounds, while
substitutions have yielded monofluoroallenes.<sup>2c,7</sup> Moreover,
the intramolecular versions of these additions and substitu-
tions allowed the construction of difluoromethylated<sup>8</sup> and
fluorinated<sup>9</sup> naphthalene nuclei.
In contrast, the cycloadditions of 1,1-difluoroallenes have
been restricted to the pioneering studies of metal-free reactions
by Dolbier<sup>2a,10</sup> and have since remained underdeveloped,
except for a Mo(CO) -catalyed reaction by Hammond.<sup>11</sup> In
recent years, our research has focused on the metal-catalysed
cycloaddition of 1,1-difluoroallenes, leading to the discovery of

difluoroallenes: past studies and recent advances.
a gold-catalysed [2+3] cycloaddition with 1,3-dipolar com-
pounds, such as nitrile- or imine oxides, to construct five-
membered ring structures (Scheme 1a).<sup>12</sup> This reaction pro-
ceeds through aurated difluoroallylic cations A with a Z
configuration,<sup>6a</sup> where the positive charge is localised owing
to the unique a-carbocation stabilising efect of the fluorine
substituents (Fig. 1).<sup>3</sup> The CF cations A were regioselectively
attacked by the oxygen<sup>6a</sup> of nitrile or imine oxides. The result-
ing adducts then underwent ring closure at the aurated carbon,
leading to the formation of ring-fluorinated isoxazole deriva-
tives (a,b-[2+3] cycloaddition).

our focus towards synthesising six-membered ring-fluorinated
heterocycles using a,b-unsaturated ketones in a [2+4] cyclo-
addition of difluoroallenes (Scheme 1b).<sup>13,14</sup> We hypothesised

fluorine substituents on a cumulated diene framework, have
emerged as highly versatile synthetic building blocks for both

properties of the fluorine substituents,<sup>3</sup> combined with the
reactive nature of the allene scafold,<sup>4</sup> enable pathways to
valuable fluorinated targets. Over the past decade, the synthetic

particularly through metal-catalysed or -promoted additions
and substitutions. For instance, additions involving carbon
and heteroatom<sup>6</sup> nucleophiles have facilitated the synthesis of

Recognising the potential of 1,1-difluoroallene cycloaddi-
tions for constructing ring-fluorinated heterocycles, we shifted
our focus towards synthesising six-membered ring-fluorinated
heterocycles using a,b-unsaturated ketones in a [2+4] cyclo-
addition of difluoroallenes (Scheme 1b).<sup>13,14</sup> We hypothesised
that treating 1,1-difluoroallenes with enones in the presence of
a gold(I) catalyst would promote the a-selective nucleophilic
attack of the enone oxygen,<sup>6a</sup> yielding the corresponding
adducts. Subsequent ring closure at the b-carbon of the enone
moiety could regio- and stereoselectively generate 3-alkylidene-

A survey of solvents, using chalcone (2d) as the enone,
identified 1,2-dichloroethane as the most efective solvent
(Table 2). When 1a was reacted with 2d in the presence of an
AuCl(IPr)–AgSbF catalyst in toluene, 3f was obtained in 3%
yield (entry 1). Performing the reaction in hexane increased the
yield of 3f to 52% (entry 2). Although the reaction reached
completion in dichloromethane, it had poor reproducibility
(entry 3), whereas in 1,2-dichloroethane, it achieved a quanti-
tative yield (entry 4). When the reaction was performed in ether,
THF and DMF, the starting difluoroallene 1a was recovered in
yields of 24–72% (entries 5–7).

corresponding ring-fluorinated difluoro(dihydro)pyrans 3b and 3c
in 83% and 97% yields, respectively. Enones 2b and 2c, featuring a
secondary alkyl group and an alkenyl group as

Nonfluorinated allene 5 did not react with chalcone (2d) in
the presence of the same AuCl(IPr)–AgSbF catalyst, leading to a
98% recovery of the starting 5 even at the reflux temperature of

the generation of the key allylic cations, i.e. A, thereby facilitat-

In summary, the [2+4] cycloaddition of 1,1-difluoroallenes
and conjugated enones successfully yielded ring-difluorinated
oxygen heterocycles. In the presence of a cationic gold(I)
catalyst, the reaction proceeded with regio- and stereoselectiv-
ities for both the difluoroallenes and enones, resulting in the
formation of six-membered products, (E)-3-alkylidene-2,2-
difluoro-3,4-dihydro-2H-pyrans, in good to excellent yields.

As expected from our former results,<sup>6a</sup> nucleophilic attack by the
oxygen atom of enones 2 occurs regioselectively at the carbon a to
the fluorine substituents, forming intermediate adducts B. Finally,
ring closure of B proceeds to yield the
\alpha , \beta { - } [ 2 { + } 4 ]

maintaining the configuration of the allylic cations A. The cationic

1,1-difluoroallenes 1 with enones 2.
Scheme 3 Control experiment with nonfluorinated allene 5.
Nonfluorinated allene 5 did not react with chalcone (2d) in
the presence of the same AuCl(IPr)–AgSbF catalyst, leading to a
98% recovery of the starting 5 even at the reflux temperature of
1,2-dichloroethane (Scheme 3). Thus, the a-carbocation stabi-
lising effect of the fluorine substituents contributed greatly to
the generation of the key allylic cations, i.e. A, thereby facilitat-
ing the synthesis of the ring-difluorinated dihydro-2H-pyrans.
In summary, the [2+4] cycloaddition of 1,1-difluoroallenes
and conjugated enones successfully yielded ring-difluorinated
oxygen heterocycles. In the presence of a cationic gold(I)
catalyst, the reaction proceeded with regio- and stereoselectiv-
ities for both the difluoroallenes and enones, resulting in the
formation of six-membered products, (E)-3-alkylidene-2,2-
difluoro-3,4-dihydro-2H-pyrans, in good to excellent yields.
